extracted.intended_audience: scholars, policymakers, and administrators concerned with science policy and peer review (researchers studying peer review, grant program managers)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes the criteria reviewers actually apply when evaluating scientific grant proposals, the common failure modes of peer review, and proposed reform principles for peer-review systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance / importance of the question
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the proposal address a problem of recognized scientific importance?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by reviewers to judge whether the research question matters to the field; higher priority given to proposals addressing pressing or widely acknowledged problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific merit and rigor of the approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Soundness of design, methods, and analysis plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate methodological appropriateness, experimental/control design, statistical or analytical rigor, and whether the methods are adequate to answer the posed question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Track record, prior publications, prior funding, ability to complete the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses the principal investigator's and team's qualifications, expertise, and demonstrated capacity to execute the proposed research and produce credible results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the proposed work can be accomplished in the time and budget specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers scope versus resources, timeline realism, and whether the plan is achievable within the proposed constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the proposal break new ground or merely incrementally extend known work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates novelty of concepts, potential for significant advance, and whether the project departs meaningfully from established lines of research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional environment and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the host institution provide adequate support?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers availability of facilities, institutional commitments, collaborators, and administrative or infrastructural support that affect project success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cronyism / 'old boy' networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers favor known researchers from elite institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as a failure mode: social networks and prestige can unduly influence favorable evaluations regardless of proposal content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservatism
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers reward incremental, safe, well-grounded proposals over genuinely novel ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A bias against risk-taking that leads to privileging incremental research and may suppress transformative or high-risk/high-reward work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias against unorthodoxy and interdisciplinary work
rubrics_metrics.description: Review processes tend to disadvantage proposals that are unorthodox or cut across disciplinary boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interdisciplinary or heterodox proposals may be misunderstood, undervalued, or judged by inappropriate disciplinary standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-serving bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may protect their own subfield's funding share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers can act to maintain resources for their community, leading to allocation decisions that reflect subfield competition rather than broader merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Halo effect from prior funding success
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful applicants get rewarded again, regardless of new proposal merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior success can create cumulative advantage: past funding or reputation colors reviewers' judgments of current proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers face no consequences for low-quality reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of mechanisms to evaluate or sanction reviewers reduces incentives for careful, well-justified reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality misused as cover for poor reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential review processes can be invoked to hide weak or unsubstantiated critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy can shelter reviewers from scrutiny, allowing unsupported judgments to stand unexamined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inability to detect fraud in submitted preliminary data
rubrics_metrics.description: Review systems are often unable to detect fraudulent or fabricated preliminary findings presented by applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits of peer review mean that falsified data or misleading preliminary results may escape detection during proposal review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency (proposed reform criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes making processes and evaluation criteria clearer to applicants and the community (e.g., open criteria, disclosure of procedures) to reduce abuse and hidden biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability (proposed reform criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement mechanisms to evaluate reviewer quality, provide feedback, and impose consequences or incentives to improve review rigor and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive reviewer perspectives (proposed reform criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer-review systems should be inclusive of diverse reviewer perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruit reviewers across disciplines, institutions, career stages, and demographics to mitigate homogeneous judgments and disciplinary parochialism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness to applicant rebuttals (proposed reform criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer-review systems should be responsive to applicant rebuttals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow applicants opportunities to respond to criticisms, clarifying misunderstandings and correcting factual errors before final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic audits for systematic bias (proposed reform criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer-review systems should be periodically audited for systematic bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct regular evaluations of review outcomes to detect and correct persistent inequities, conservatisms, or other systemic problems.
